summary.headline: Late-payment and compliance workflow services look strongest in the UK right now, with invoice-chasing automation the cleanest fast-cash offer.
summary.best_opportunity: Invoice chasing and cash-collection automation for UK SMEs.
summary.why_now: A current GOV.UK Commercial Payments Bill overview says late payments cost the UK economy £11 billion per year, see 38 UK businesses close every day, and the bill will impose 60-day maximum payment terms and mandate late-payment interest at 8% above the Bank of England base rate. That makes cash-collection pain immediate, measurable and easy to sell against.

top_opportunities.name: Invoice chasing and cash-collection automation for SMEs
top_opportunities.description: A productized service or narrow micro-SaaS that sends staged reminders, tracks replies, escalates exceptions and gives owners a simple overdue-cash dashboard across Xero, QuickBooks or spreadsheets.
top_opportunities.why_now: A live GOV.UK Commercial Payments Bill overview says late payments cost the UK economy £11 billion per year, see 38 UK businesses close every day, and the bill will impose 60-day maximum payment terms while mandating interest at 8% above the Bank of England base rate. The pain is already active, and the ROI is money already earned.
top_opportunities.buyer: UK agencies, consultancies, recruiters, trades, wholesalers and other SMEs with manual receivables processes.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £250-£1,000 for accounting integrations, reminder flows, a small dashboard and outbound prospecting.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Very fast; a setup fee plus first-month retainer is plausible inside 1-2 weeks.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High via monthly monitoring, reminder handling and escalation support.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Excellent for a solo engineer because the offer can start as workflow glue and service, not a full finance platform.
risks: Accounting products already include basic reminders, so the wedge needs sharper escalation logic or vertical focus.
Some buyers will ask for contingency or success-fee pricing, which can complicate margins.
top_opportunities.verdict: Best overall today because the buyer pain is current, the commercial outcome is obvious and the offer can be sold service-first on a small budget.

top_opportunities.name: Companies House identity-verification workflow service for accountants and corporate service firms
top_opportunities.description: A workflow tool or managed service that collects director data, tracks who has verified, runs reminder sequences and handles bulk admin around Companies House identity checks.
top_opportunities.why_now: Current GOV.UK guidance says identity verification became a legal requirement from 18 November 2025 and marks the start of a 12-month transition period. That creates real administrative workload now for firms handling many entities.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small accountancy firms, corporate service providers, formation agents and outsourced company secretarial teams.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £300-£1,400 for secure intake forms, reminder logic, status tracking and a lightweight dashboard.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Fast as a done-for-you setup or workflow-management offer.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium to high if extended into annual company-secretarial and filing admin.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Very good for a solo engineer who can build secure operational tooling without offering regulated advice.
risks: Handling identity-related data raises trust and security requirements immediately.
Standalone verification demand may taper unless bundled into broader ongoing company-secretarial workflows.
top_opportunities.verdict: Strong near-term opportunity because the legal trigger is live and the work is operational rather than speculative.

top_opportunities.name: Productized AI workflow automation for operationally stretched SMEs
top_opportunities.description: A fixed-scope service that maps one repetitive workflow, automates the handoffs and adds AI only where it removes admin or speeds decisions.
top_opportunities.why_now: Current search-result pages still surface GOV.UK AI guidance and AI adoption research for UK businesses, which suggests live interest, but the evidence is weaker than the compliance-led ideas above. The opportunity is best when sold around one workflow and one ROI claim, not generic AI transformation.
top_opportunities.buyer: Owner-led SMEs, recruiters, brokers, accountants, small professional-services firms and multi-site local businesses with repetitive back-office work.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200-£1,200 using existing LLM APIs, automation tooling, a simple demo and direct outreach.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Fast if sold as a paid audit plus implementation rather than SaaS-first.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High through support retainers, monitoring and incremental workflow expansions.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Excellent for a solo software engineer who can scope tightly and ship one automation at a time.
risks: Generic AI-agency positioning is crowded and weak.
Buyers may want education and ROI proof before they buy, which lengthens some sales.
top_opportunities.verdict: Still attractive, but only with hard productization and a niche workflow wedge because broad AI offers are too fuzzy.

top_opportunities.name: Missed-call recovery and quote follow-up automation for trades and appointment-led local SMEs
top_opportunities.description: A productized service that captures missed calls, sends instant SMS or WhatsApp follow-up, books appointments and nudges dormant quotes until they convert or close out.
top_opportunities.why_now: The current ServiceM8 UK site says businesses using the platform complete 30% more work in the first 3 months and that users manage over £18B in jobs through the platform. That is not policy-level evidence, but it is a live signal that trades and service businesses pay for operational tooling tied to revenue and throughput.
top_opportunities.buyer: Trades, garages, clinics, salons, dentists and other owner-led service businesses that rely on inbound phone leads.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200-£1,200 for telephony APIs, messaging flows, CRM glue and reporting.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Very fast with a setup fee plus monthly support or per-number pricing.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High because numbers, messaging and monitoring fit monthly billing naturally.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Excellent for a solo engineer comfortable with webhooks, telephony and lightweight AI summaries.
risks: This category is getting crowded, so vertical specialization matters.
Evidence is market-activity rather than a regulatory trigger, so demand varies more by niche.
top_opportunities.verdict: Probably the quickest local-sales offer if positioned around recovered leads for one niche.

top_opportunities.name: Making Tax Digital workflow automation for small accountancy and bookkeeping firms
top_opportunities.description: A workflow layer that handles client onboarding, document chasing, reminder sequences, exception tracking and internal task routing around Making Tax Digital admin.
top_opportunities.why_now: The current GOV.UK guidance page for using Making Tax Digital for Income Tax was updated on 16 July 2026, and current search-result pages for the topic are dominated by software-choice and compatibility content. That suggests active market motion now, although today’s direct evidence is weaker than the late-payment and Companies House signals above.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small UK accountancy firms, bookkeepers and tax advisers serving sole traders and landlords.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £300-£1,500 for a demo workflow, landing page, outreach and a few integrations.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Fast as a done-for-you setup or migration-admin service.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High through ongoing reminder management, exception handling and per-client workflow retainers.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Very good for a solo engineer because the offer can sit on top of existing practice software instead of replacing it.
risks: Core tax software is crowded, so the wedge must stay on workflow admin and client chasing.
Today’s live evidence supports active market interest, but the urgency signal is less explicit than the bill and identity-verification pages.
top_opportunities.verdict: Still credible, especially for an engineer with accounting contacts, but it ranks slightly lower today because the live urgency signal was softer.

best_pick.name: Invoice chasing and cash-collection automation for SMEs
best_pick.why_it_wins: It matches the brief better than the others: low build cost, part-time friendly delivery, clear immediate ROI, broad buyer pool and an easy path from setup fee to monthly retainer. The current GOV.UK payment-policy signal also makes the pain timely without needing buyers to believe in a speculative future trend.
validation_plan: Build one demo flow connected to a fake invoice ledger showing first reminder, second reminder, escalation and owner alerting.
Contact 30 UK agencies, consultancies and recruiters that mention cash-flow pressure, late payment or finance admin in reviews or job posts.
Offer a fixed-price pilot for one receivables workflow and measure recovered cash, time saved and average days-to-payment over 30 days.
best_pick.first_offer: £500-£1,250 setup for one receivables workflow plus £99-£299 per month for monitoring, reminders and exception handling.
best_pick.mvp: A lightweight dashboard plus automated email and SMS reminder sequences, overdue segmentation, response logging and manual-escalation hooks on top of Xero, QuickBooks or CSV imports.
best_pick.do_today: Ship a one-page offer, record a 2-minute demo of an overdue-invoice flow and build an outreach list of 30 UK SMEs with obvious receivables friction.
